elements.element: Customer is not obligated to use Vendor as its exclusive or sole supplier.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 now makes Vendor only “a provider” and expressly states that Customer remains free to obtain analytics or other services from any third party at any time. Section 12.3 also states that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, its scope is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Sections 2.2 and 12.3 establish that Customer has no exclusivity obligation at all.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, its duration is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause imposes no exclusivity obligation on Customer.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer is not subject to exclusivity; therefore no performance-based release is needed.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer is not subject to exclusivity; therefore no delivery-based release is needed.

result.reason: The operative language fully removes the sole-supplier obligation and affirmatively preserves Customer's right to use third parties, so it satisfies the preferred position and necessarily exceeds the fallback protections. The edit is not strictly minimal because it adds a minimum-volume statement that is unnecessary to eliminate exclusivity and duplicates Section 12.3. The language is otherwise clear, consistent, and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
